newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Violence rages on in riot-torn French Guiana.
newsitem.headline: Violence rages on in riot-torn French Guiana.

text.p: Roving gangs of rioting youths roamed the city of Cayenne in French Guiana late on Tuesday, burning tires and throwing Molotov cocktail firebombs, witnesses said.

Explosions were heard at 10 p.m. local time (0100 GMT Wednesday). Smoke from burning tires entered into homes blocks away from the centres of violence. Riot police countered with tear gas grenades, witnesses said.

Local state-owned radio said several rioters were seen with pump-action rifles. Some local journalists and photographers were attacked by the rioters in a new wave of violence in the French overseas territory on the northeast coast of South America.
During a first wave of rioting and looting last week, 40 rifles were stolen from a sports shop causing alarm in the population and authorities.
Fresh violence erupted on Tuesday when a magistrate's court convicted seven people arrested during riots last week, witnesses said.

At the announcement of the verdict, bands of youths overturned garbage cans, smashed store windows and attempted to charge the local courthouse. Riot police fired several rounds of tear gas to disperse the crowd, which had massed near the courthouse all day.

Two hundred paramilitary riot police reinforcements were flown to French Guiana from Paris over the weekend. They supplemented local police who have been overwhelmed by the riots that killed one person, injured at least seven and caused millions of dollars of damage to government buildings and to stores on Thursday and Friday nights.
Airport officials told Reuters all incoming and outgoing flights at French Guiana's international airport near Cayenne would be cancelled on Wednesday.

The airport closure was triggered by a general strike called for on Wednesday by an inter-union group protesting against French government policy in French Guiana and the arrest of the seven rioters convicted on Tuesday.
High school students protesting against poor conditions in local schools sparked the riots when their strike degenerated into clashes between police and youths.
Earlier on Tuesday, the French government said in Paris that it would hold wide-ranging talks next year on the situation in French Guiana.

Jean-Jacques de Peretti, minister of overseas territories, said he would visit Guiana in the near future with Education Minister Francois Bayrou and organise a conference there next year, "because the future of the Guianese is a matter for the Guianese themselves."
De Peretti told the National Assembly that the problems of French Guiana stemmed largely from illegal immigration and a sharp increase in population to 140,000 from 80,000 over the past 13 years.

French Guiana is the only dependent territory in South America. Its economy lags behind that of mainland France, and it has an unemployment rate approaching 25 percent of the labour force. Joblessness is particularly acute among the young.
